entries.answer: Time is the ordering of events, and the ordinary question of what time it is needs a live clock, which this bank does not have. I can explain how time is measured, why time zones exist, and how to read any clock you are given, but I will not invent a reading. If you need the time, look at a device; it is faster than anything I could say and it is right.

entries.answer: A time zone is a region whose clocks agree, and the offsets from Greenwich range from about minus twelve to plus fourteen, which is why it is nearly always wrong to guess. The reason the offsets are not whole hours is that they are political: a zone boundary is usually a border, and when one moves its clocks the neighbours have to agree. The Philippines is eight hours ahead of Greenwich and does not use daylight saving, which is a useful fact for anyone catching up with a call.

patterns: does the philippines use daylight saving
entries.answer: Daylight saving time is the practice of moving clocks forward in summer so that evenings are lighter, and the stated reason is saving energy on lighting. The evidence for the energy saving is weak, and the real effects are a lost hour in spring and a repeated hour in autumn. The Philippines does not observe it, and neither do most of Asia, which leaves the country permanently out of step with Europe and North America for half the year.

patterns: why are there 7 days in a week
entries.answer: A calendar is a system for dividing time into countable units, and the one in use is built from astronomy that was settled long before it. Months come from lunar cycles, which is why their lengths are irregular, while the week is seven days for a historical reason that has no astronomical support at all. The awkward parts are inherited: leap years, months with thirty days, and a year that does not divide evenly into anything.

patterns: how to read a train timetable
entries.answer: A timetable is a published schedule of when something happens, and the word is most used for transport where the times are fixed and the service runs whether or not you need it. It is a different object from a calendar, which organises your own time, and from a schedule, which is a plan somebody arranges. Reading one properly means looking for the change times rather than the departure times, since those are the ones that catch people out.
